newsitem.title: USA: Memberworks flat after IPO market debut.
newsitem.headline: Memberworks flat after IPO market debut.

text.p: MemberWorks Inc shares were flat after the company's market debut as analysts fretted over the company's short-term profitability weakness.

The company's shares closed at $17 after pricing at the high end of their estimated pricing range of $15 to $17 a share. The Stanford, Connecticut-based company provides membership service programs. As of June 30, 1996, it had about 40 client organizations and 1.5 million members.

"Their uniqueness is their ability to find these niches and carve them out, which is very good, but their weakness is they haven't made much money yet," said Manish Shah of the IPO Maven. "It's disappinting, but in about two years, they could deliver a major upside of profitability and revenues,"
Shah said the company could gain some business momentum and profitability after it stabilized and began widening its services to members.
"So I wouldnt jump and buy it now, but I would definitely watch it," he said.
